chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ṣāliḥ ibn al-Sindī, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Abī Salamah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

We are those whose obedience Allah has made obligatory. The people have no choice except our recognition, and the people are not excused for ignorance of us. Whoever recognizes us is a believer, and whoever denies us is a disbeliever; and whoever neither recognizes us nor denies us is astray until he returns to the guidance that Allah has made obligatory upon him, namely our obligatory obedience. So if he dies upon his misguidance, Allah will do with him whatever He wills.

key_terms.الْهُدَى: guidance; the right path ordained by Allah
key_terms.بِجَهَالَتِنَا: through ignorance of us; lack of knowledge concerning the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.ضَالًّا: astray; misguided and not upon right guidance
key_terms.طَاعَتَنَا: our obedience; obedience owed to the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.فَرَضَ: made obligatory; imposed as a divine duty
key_terms.كَافِرًا: a disbeliever; one who rejects and thereby falls into kufr
key_terms.مَعْرِفَتُنَا: recognition of us; acknowledging and knowing the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.مُؤْمِنًا: a believer; one counted among the people of iman

ai.seo_question: What does al-Kāfī say about the obligation of recognizing and obeying the Imams عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms that obedience to the Imams عليهم السلام is divinely mandated and that recognizing their authority is not optional for people. It distinguishes between the believer who knows them, the disbeliever who rejects them, and the one who remains astray through lack of recognition until he returns to the guidance of their obligatory obedience.
